full_judgment:
Syed Mohammad Hussain, J: In these three rules the concurrent decision of both the courts below allowing pre-emption cases under section 96, of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is under challenge. 

 3. Although there is no fixed period" under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as to how long a pre-emptor can afford to remain ignorant about any transfer over which pre-emption can be claimed, such question must be adjudicated in a reasonable manner so that no owner of property suffers from any insecurity and threat to his ownership even after a period of over a decade when someone can claim such property by way of a right of pre-emption on the ground that one had no knowledge about a transfer taking place over a period of one decade. In order to decide this question in the present case certain admitted facts will have to be considered. The pre-emptors and the pre-emptees have cultivable lands contiguous to each other without any intervention by any third person and such lands are being cultivated both by the pre-emptors and the pre-emptees for over a decade. Further the pre emptors and the pre-emptees are living in houses intervened six other houses in between them in the same village within the same locality. Both the pre-emptors and pre emptees are paying rents to the same settlement office for over a decade In considering such facts it must be held that the pre-emptors and the pre-emptee having lived together side by side and having cultivated lands contiguous to each other for over a decade such preemptors and pre-emptees cannot be called strangers to each other. The very purpose of law of pre-emption is to avoid stranger amongst the same group of co- sharers. The present pre-emptors and pre-emptees both being co-sharers to the same holding together for over a decade, the pre-emptors claiming seniority over pre-emprees by few months only, none of them being stranger to each other are common co-sharers for over a decade the very principle of application for pre-emption is not applicable in the present case. For the foregoing reason s it was wrong on the part of the courts below to accept the plea of the pre-emptors that they had no knowledge of the transfer of land taking place nearly about 12 years before. Such ignorance cannot be arrogated to any person of prudence and common sense. Further, it will endanger the security of holding of any person who has held and cultivated a land for over a decade and such land is being claimed by a person who lives as an immediate neighbor and a contiguous owner of a land for over a decade. Be that as it may for the foregoing reasons the impugned decisions of both the courts below allowing the applications for pre-emption under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act in the present cases must be held to have suffered from clear error of law and are accordingly set aside. The pre-emption cases stand dismissed.
